discussion_comments.comment_body: tool and compaction entries can now also have usage. need to account for that. same for memory and other storage.

I was randomly looking at recent commits in this project in preparation for doing some myself, and this chunk of code *really* jumped out.

Like here we are in a core file operation "check if a file exists" and we fall back to this MacOS screenshot-specific heuristic of replacing AM/PM etc?

I mean, it should *at least* conditionalize on being on MacOS right?

But even there, again to me the idea of just falling back to looking for a different filename like this feels way too janky/heuristic to live in something core. The possible set of heuristics here when one considers all kinds of Unicode is virtually unbounded.

If this MacOS screenshot is a common problem for you it seems simpler to just tell the LLM "load the file with a similar name" or so...

Backslash-escaped quotes in normalizeNulRedirects: Added an isEscaped() helper that counts consecutive backslashes before a quote character. Quotes now only toggle state when they are not escaped. This correctly handles \" (literal quote inside or outside double quotes) while preserving bash semantics where inside single quotes backslash has no special meaning.
Need to check if it's correct to remove the `{granularity:"grapheme"}` from this instance.

[grapheme granularity is the default](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/Segmenter/Segmenter#options), but I'll refactor this back so that it maintains the original style.
